title: Normalized divisor equations, associated lines, and flat pullback
statement: Let $X,Y$ be algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], with divisors and local rational coefficients [def-sfb-space-divisors] and total fractions [def-sfb-space-total-fractions]. Use flatness on etale scheme charts [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] and the canonical tensor-pullback functor, adjunction unit, and local tensor sections [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. For a fraction $g=a/b$ on an affine chart and a codimension-one point $y$, define its order as $\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_y/(a))-\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_y/(b))$; on regular charts this is the normalized DVR valuation. A Weil divisor corresponds to a Cartier divisor if on every affine chart where $g$ is an equation its coefficient at every codimension-one point is this order. A rationally trivialized line $(L,s)$ is associated to Cartier data $D$ if it embeds as an $\mathcal O_X$-module into $\mathcal K_X$ and locally has a regular frame $e$ and an equation $g$ of $D$ with $s=g e$ and $e\mapsto g^{-1}$. Thus locally $L=g^{-1}\mathcal O_X$ and $s\mapsto1$. For a flat map $q:X\to Y$, every compatible affine etale chart triangle has flat coordinate map $A\to B$, which preserves non-zero-divisors. Its fraction map sends $a/b$ to $q(a)/q(b)$. Cartier data $E$ is the flat pullback of $D$ when each local equation pulls back by this map. A rational section $t$ is the flat pullback of $s$ if on every such chart triangle, whenever $s=g e$ in a regular frame, $t=q(g)(1\otimes e)$, with $1\otimes e$ formed using the fixed tensor-pullback adjunction unit. No dimension hypothesis or arbitrary comparison map is included.
